lines.text: A lot of companies are trying to decide between doing SOC 2 or ISO.
In a nutshell, SOC 2 is geared around data security.
There's availability, integrity, privacy, confidentiality, and of course, data security.
Data security is the minimum required from a SOC 2 perspective.
ISO is recognized by international companies.
SOC 2 is geared for service providers.
It's recognized by the U.S. or a lot of U.S. companies.
But when you're trying to decide whether to do SOC 2 or ISO, really it should come down to what your customer is asking for.
There's maybe 60 to 80% overlap, but they're a different type of work.
ISO, I believe, is a little harder to do because there's a lot of policy and governance and whatnot, but it can be straightforward for the right company.
If you have international customers, ISO is going to be much more recognized.
It's not going to hurt you to do both.
